paper: Kavvas et al. 2018 Nat Commun, s41467-018-06634-y, PMID 30333483

central_claims_tested.claim: ML approach recovers known AMR genes
central_claims_tested.test: Cross-check Table 1 known-AMR genes against MI top-40 (MOESM4) + SVM (MOESM5)
central_claims_tested.result: 14/18 top-tier (77.8%); 27/33 in full 254-gene AMR panel (MOESM9) exact match; ~28/33 accounting for case-mismatch = 85%

central_claims_tested.claim: MI ranks canonical drug targets high in AMR-associated allele lists
central_claims_tested.test: For 8 drugs, check rank of canonical drug-target gene in MI top-40
central_claims_tested.result: 3/8 rank-1; 6/8 top-5. rpoB dominance across drugs is expected (MDR co-occurrence) and matches paper narrative

central_claims_tested.claim: LOR sign matches AMR label for identified alleles
central_claims_tested.test: For all 809 R/S alleles in MOESM9, verify LOR>0 for R and LOR<0 for S

central_claims_tested.claim: Allele sequences match real M.tb H37Rv proteins
central_claims_tested.test: Fetch 6 canonical AMR gene wildtype proteins from NCBI; compare to top-pident MOESM9 alleles
central_claims_tested.result: 5/6 exact match (katG, pncA, inhA, rpsL @100%; gyrA @99.9%); rpoB cluster picked a truncated variant (known issue with reference-agnostic clustering)

central_claims_tested.test: Load MOESM7 (307 candidate interactions), apply BH correction at α=0.05
central_claims_tested.result: 232 pass BH; every paper-specifically-mentioned pair (embB-ubiA, ubiA-embR, katG-oxcA, katG-inhA, gyrA-ansP2) is confirmed with p<0.05

central_claims_tested.test: Check MOESM9 for Table 2's 23 new genes
